title: IITM Research Initiatives Spotlight -Center for Soft & Biological Matter -Advanced Materials Cluster
description: Soft-matter concerns study of a wide range of materials that can be made to flow or subjected to changes in phase or shape when an energy of the order of few times thermal energy is supplied to them. Such materials include colloids, polymers, polymers, proteins, and other small molecules or a combination of these. One of the focus area of this center will be investigation of evaporation of of complex fluids, which is a simple and inexpensive method to coat a variety of substances such as nanoparticles, microspheres, polymers, proteins, DNA and constituents of bio-fluids on solid substrates. Upon complete evaporation of solvent from complex fluids, the deposits that form are typically referred to as “evaporative patterns”. Controlling/engineering the patterns and structures formed by the evaporation of drops and films has many industrial, biomedical and engineering applications in addition to understanding the fundamental physics and processes involved.
